policy: An object description, primary text, policy announcement, statutory direction, interview statement and alleged covert operation answer different questions. Limited access is retained. Neither a government allegation nor the author's theological interpretation becomes an adjudicated fact by inclusion.

sources.title: Daniel 7, World English Bible
sources.scope: Verses 17 and 23 distinguish kings and kingdom. This is textual support for examining different levels of imagery, not a named modern identification.

sources.title: Daniel 11, World English Bible
sources.scope: Verses 36-39 and their god-of-fortresses wording. The attempted separate KJV query failed; the chapter's translated wording is not presented as a new Hebrew lexical study.

sources.title: Daniel 3, World English Bible
sources.scope: The image, worship command and furnace sanction. The text does not explicitly call the image a portrait of the king.

sources.title: Revelation 13, World English Bible
sources.scope: Distinct agents, image, consequences for refusal and the purchasing condition. It does not name contemporary policy instruments.

sources.title: Revelation 19, World English Bible
sources.scope: Verse 20 relates the false prophet to signs, the mark and the image. The modern media comparison is a further interpretation.

sources.title: Revelation 18, World English Bible
sources.scope: The commodity list, commercial participants and human lives. Different actors are not silently collapsed into a single person.

sources.title: Revelation 21, World English Bible
sources.scope: Verses 18-21 use gold in the renewed city's description; this supplies a textual control against an invariant gold-equals-evil code.

sources.title: Deuteronomy 6, World English Bible
sources.scope: Verse 8's hand and between-the-eyes sign. A relationship with Revelation is a proposed intertext, not a claim the passage explicitly explains John's intention.

sources.title: Revelation 14, World English Bible
sources.scope: Verse 1's forehead names provide an internal comparison with the beast's mark.

sources.title: 1 Corinthians 10, World English Bible
sources.scope: Verses 14-28 distinguish ritual participation, market purchases and a stated sacrificial origin. One letter is not a census of all Roman cities.

sources.title: Pliny, Letters 10.96, Dickinson College Commentaries
sources.kind: Latin primary text with scholarly notes
sources.scope: Sections 3-10 on questioning, imperial images, release, punishment and sacrificial trade. The commentary includes competing assessments; none turns the text into a universal commerce law.

sources.title: Trajan's reply, Pliny Letters 10.97, Dickinson College Commentaries
sources.kind: Latin primary text with scholarly notes
sources.scope: Limits on seeking out Christians and anonymous denunciations, with the stated conditions of punishment and pardon.

sources.title: Didache, chapters 5 and 11, translation hosted by New Advent
sources.scope: The Way of Death and tests involving prophetic conduct. The wider ethical and ritual work is not reduced to one modern political program.

sources.title: Royal Society of Chemistry, Gold
sources.scope: Material properties; no psychological intention is inferred from a material's use.

sources.title: Royal Society of Chemistry, Osmium
sources.scope: Density comparison correcting the assertion that gold is the heaviest or densest element.

sources.title: Chateau de Versailles, Restoration of Apollo's fountain
sources.scope: Apollo as a royal allegory and the gilded lead fountain. A historical allegory is not evidence of an identical intention in every later display.

sources.title: Joyce Chen, Donald Trump's Extravagant, Gold-Rimmed NYC Penthouse, Us Weekly, November 11, 2015
sources.scope: Reported gold/marble, Greek mythology and Louis XIV-style decoration. Property valuations, exact dimensions and artist provenance are not adopted as independently authenticated.

sources.title: Face of Malawi, Trump Tower penthouse feature, November 16, 2016
sources.scope: Indexed text identifies Apollo and Aurora above a fireplace. Direct page access returned 403. This low-confidence artwork-provenance lead does not establish a cult, an artist or the owner's stated intent.

sources.title: CNN, Flags, figurines and gold everywhere, March 16, 2025, hosted by KTVZ
sources.scope: The objects, gilded features and reported decorating choices. Descriptive rhetoric is not adopted as an assessment of political leadership or private motives.

sources.scope: The release's alleged funding and direction, and its explicit presumption-of-innocence notice. This pass does not establish subsequent case disposition or the knowledge of every content participant.

sources.scope: Date and proposed prohibition/pause structure. The office's examples, allegations and policy judgments are not independently authenticated by their inclusion in the release.

sources.title: Paul Mullins, The Triumph of Tackiness: The Materiality of Trump, November 22, 2016
sources.kind: Named author's material-culture essay and photograph caption
sources.scope: The Apollo-in-chariot caption and separate discussion of ceiling paintings were read. They are not a catalogue attribution of a particular Reni copy or proof of worship. The essay's political evaluations are not adopted here.

sources.title: Sword of the Word Apologetics w/ Zach, The AntiChrist Template: Apollo & Trump. The Bloodline of AntiChrist
sources.kind: Primary publication of an eschatological interpretation
sources.scope: Publicly readable title, prose description and February 24 label were consulted; no year appeared in the retrieved header. No full video or subscriber-only material was reviewed. Political or supernatural conclusions are attributed to the author, not adopted as findings.

sources.title: r/Christianity, Is DJT the antichrist? supplied discussion
sources.scope: Apollo and god-of-fortresses comments were located in the supplied thread. Relative age labels are not silently converted to exact dates. Comments establish that interpretations were expressed, not that an artwork attribution or religious claim is true.

sources.title: Aeschylus, Agamemnon, translated by E. D. A. Morshead, Internet Classics Archive
sources.kind: Ancient literary text in an identified English translation
sources.scope: Cassandra's Apollo/destroyer invocations, corresponding to Greek lines approximately 1080-1086, were read. The consulted translation is not a new critical Greek edition or evidence of a modern religious affiliation.

sources.title: Plato, Cratylus, translated by Benjamin Jowett, Internet Classics Archive
sources.scope: Discussion around 404e-406a of the destructive association and alternative explanations of Apollo's name was consulted. The dialogue's etymological play is not presented as modern linguistic proof of every derivation.

sources.title: Revelation 9, World English Bible
sources.scope: The fifth and sixth trumpet units, verses 1-19, were read, including the nonlethal restriction, five months, the naming in verse 11 and the later cavalry. A theological combination of actors is not treated as an explicit verse-level identity.

sources.title: Revelation 9:11 Greek text and morphological display, Bible Hub
sources.kind: Greek editions reproduced with morphological aids
sources.scope: Apollyon and Abaddon in the displayed Greek were consulted. No exhaustive manuscript collation or claim about an unverified variant reading Apollo is made.

sources.title: Apollyon, Strong's Greek 623 with Thayer material
sources.scope: The derivation of Apollyon from the language of destroying was consulted. Site-generated commentary and an assumption that every named destructive figure is Satan are not adopted as lexical facts.

sources.title: Roma Capitale, Casino dell'Aurora Pallavicini: Guido Reni's masterpiece shines again
sources.scope: The original fresco's Rome location, commission and distinct figures were consulted. The account does not authenticate a particular work in Trump Tower, and dated visiting hours are not reused as current advice.

sources.title: Shannon Pritchard, Guido Reni, Aurora, Smarthistory
sources.scope: Aurora, Apollo and the torch-bearing Phosphorus are identified separately. This interpretation concerns the Rome fresco, not a full provenance study of the reported penthouse decoration.

sources.title: Isaiah 14, World English Bible
sources.scope: Verse 4's stated addressee and verse 12's morning-star/son-of-dawn language. No claim of an explicit Eos or Apollo name in the Hebrew passage is made.

sources.title: Daniel 11:38 Hebrew text and translation comparison, Bible Hub
sources.kind: Hebrew text with morphological and translation aids
sources.scope: Ma'uzzim and al-kanno were compared with the displayed translations. This does not identify a specific deity or turn the KJV word estate into an explicit prediction of a luxury residence.

sources.title: Homer, Iliad 1, A. T. Murray translation, Theoi Classical Texts Library
sources.scope: Lines 8-52, Apollo's plague and arrows, were consulted. A destructive narrative role does not by itself identify the deity of Daniel 11:38.
